st: Wear gloves when peeling the taro, as raw taro can irritate the skin. Cut it into even cubes.
Put the taro in a pot with [[4 cups]] water and the salt. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the taro is very soft when pierced.
Drain well and mash with a potato masher until thick and smooth.
Stir in half the coconut milk and the sugar. Mix to a thick pudding that holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Briefly warm the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water to make them bend without tearing.
Line a baking dish with the leaves or foil. Spoon in the taro mixture and smooth the top.
Pour the remaining coconut milk over the top and bake for 30 minutes until the surface is set and lightly browned.
Cool for 10 minutes and serve warm, cut into squares.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). In place of a stone oven, a covered roasting pan will steam the food.
Season the pork and fish with the salt and pepper. Warm the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water so they bend easily.
Line a deep roasting pan with half the leaves, letting them hang over the sides. Pour in [[1 cup]] water.
Layer the pork and the taro on the leaves first, since they take the longest to cook.
Add the sweet potatoes and then the fish on top. Pour the coconut milk over everything.
Fold the overhanging leaves over the food and cover with the remaining leaves. Seal the pan tightly with foil.
Bake for 2.5 hours until the pork is tender and reaches at least 145°F/63°C and the roots are soft.
Let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes before opening, as hot steam will escape.
Serve on the leaves, with the juices spooned over.

ing: such as snapper, cut into large pieces
st: Rub the fish with the lime juice and half the salt. Set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and chili and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and the remaining salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, but do not boil hard.
Slide the fish into the sauce in a single layer. Spoon the sauce over it.
Cover and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (145°F/63°C).
Taste and adjust the salt. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with rice or boiled root vegetables and lime wedges.

ing: slippery cabbage, or spinach and bok choy
st: Wash the greens well and chop them into bite-size pieces. Keep the tender stems separate from the leaves.
Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the stems, the water and the salt. Cover and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the leaves and pour in the coconut milk.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are soft and the sauce is slightly creamy.
Taste, add pepper and more salt if needed and serve warm as a side.

ing: peeled and finely grated, or use thawed frozen grated cassava
st: Peel the cassava, cutting out the woody core, and grate it finely. Squeeze the pulp in a clean towel to remove extra liquid.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Warm the banana leaves over a flame to soften them.
Grease a baking dish with the butter and line it with the leaves or parchment.
Mix the cassava with the coconut milk, sugar, grated coconut and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the mixture into the dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 50 minutes until the top is golden and a knife comes out clean from the center.
Cool for 15 minutes so the pudding sets, then cut into squares and serve warm or at room temperature.
Rub the whole breadfruit with the oil. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C), or prepare a hot charcoal fire.
Roast the whole breadfruit on a baking sheet for 50 minutes, turning once, until the skin is charred and a knife goes in easily.
Let it cool for 10 minutes. Cut it open, remove the core and peel off the charred skin.
Cut the flesh into thick slices or large chunks.
Meanwhile, simmer the coconut milk, onion and salt in a small pot for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the flaked fish and warm for 2 minutes.
Arrange the breadfruit on a plate and spoon the hot coconut cream over it.
